plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000-gene salmon-quantified counts for 1 treated and 1 control human liver sample (metadata.csv, 2x2), with no biological replication in either arm. Per the grounded procedure (Inflexa knowledge service, rule R-0003), a design with one sample per group provides no within-group variance estimate, so no valid p-value or FDR-adjusted inferential test can be produced — running DESeq2's Wald test here would report significance that has no statistical basis. The plan therefore: (1) profiles sample structure descriptively (library size, count distributions — a 2-sample PCA/vst-blind is degenerate but computed for completeness), (2) filters low-count genes, (3) computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors and normalized counts, (4) reports genes ranked by descriptive (unshrunken) log2 fold change treated vs control with no p-values or significance calls, explicitly flagging the design limitation, (5) runs an over-representation enrichment (clusterProfiler `enricher`, tested-gene universe, MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, followed by Reactome as a second collection) on a discrete list of genes with the largest descriptive fold changes, treated as hypothesis-generating only, and (6) assembles a report with full reproducibility record, explicit design caveats, and named thresholds/collections. This sequence follows the Inflexa-grounded procedure for a bulk RNA-seq, no-replicate, two-condition, human, salmon-derived-count situation, with the enrichment method constrained by the knowledge-check to over-representation analysis with an explicit universe (fgsea preranked GSEA and GO/enrichGO were both rejected as impermissible methods for this flagged, non-replicated design).
